in 1927 with Mount Rushmore being built President Coolidge and his wife took a trip to the Black Hills, Governor Bulow had heard that Coolidge was a fisherman and South Dakota was well known for its excellent trout fishing. Bulow of course saw this as an opportunity for publicity and unbeknownst to Coolidge decided to stage a fishing trip.

>Bulow and his fish warden hatched a plan [..] Nightcrawlers had been feed their own special diet, milk and oatmeal, so that worms twelve inches long would bait the presidential hook. At the state's Spearfish hatchery swam thousands of ancient, fat, trout, fish so domesticated they could hardly be likened to the wild trout of the stream. Some of them were fifteen years old. The warden's deputies netted hundreds of the hatchery fish and put them into trucks, then transported them by night to the president's pond. They also stretched a wire net [..] and unloaded the fish between nets.

They got their publicity photos however they did not pull one over on Coolidge. Later Colonel Starling ordered Bulow to dinner with the president a 50 mile trip.

>At dinner that night, Bulow came face-to-face with the harvest of his own scheming. There upon his plate lay a trout, not just any trout but one of the old hatchery liver0feds that he and the parks men had dumped in Coolidge's creek area. [..] Two Brandies were not enough to handle the fish. As the President tucked in the governor struck up a conversation with the fish: "Seems to me I've seen you before". What was that? the president asked. [...] "on the first bite I could taste the ground horse meat upon which the trout had lived for years" he later recalled.

Of course after dinner Coolidge and Bulow became fast friends with Bulow who was a democrat remarking that he would have to vote for Coolidge (of course Coolidge chose not to run that election).
